layer1_evidence.interpretation_en: A 39-year-old woman has a right breast mass at the 9 o'clock position that increased from approximately 1.5 cm to 2 cm over four months, with well-defined margins and good mobility. She was admitted for excision and diagnosis. This supports interval growth but does not establish benignity or malignancy.

The current plan is mammography-guided hook-wire localization followed by quadrant excision of the right breast calcified lesion with frozen-section examination. Breast-conserving surgery, sentinel lymph node biopsy, or more extensive surgery is conditional on a malignant result. This defines the current diagnostic intervention and pathology-dependent next steps.

Ultrasound shows an approximately 17 mm nodule at the 9 o'clock position of the right breast, assessed as category 4A on routine ultrasound and favored to be category 3 after contrast enhancement, with fibroadenoma considered first. No abnormally enlarged axillary or supraclavicular lymph nodes are seen. The imaging suggests limited to intermediate suspicion but cannot replace histologic diagnosis.

Mammography assesses the right upper-outer-quadrant mass as category 4A and clustered patchy calcifications posterior to the right nipple as category 3, requiring correlation with palpation and ultrasonography. This supports localization, excision, and pathologic confirmation of the calcified lesion but does not diagnose malignancy.

layer1_evidence.interpretation_en: A 39-year-old woman has a right-breast mass at the 9 o'clock position that enlarged from approximately 1.5 cm to 2 cm over 4 months; it is well circumscribed and mobile, and she was admitted for excision and diagnosis.

Mammography assessed the right-breast mass as category 4A; clustered patchy calcifications posterior to the right nipple were category 3 and required correlation with palpation and ultrasonography.

Intraoperative frozen section showed adenosis with fibroadenoma formation in the 9 o'clock mass and a benign calcified lesion in the upper-outer region, considered an adenomyoepithelioma with sclerosing adenosis, ductal dilatation, and a small amount of microcalcification; adjacent tissue also showed benign changes. This supports no malignancy identified on frozen section, but frozen section is not equivalent to final permanent pathology.
Right-breast quadrantectomy was completed under general anesthesia, and the mass, upper-outer calcification focus, and adjacent tissue were submitted separately for examination.

Mammography-guided hook-wire localization of the clustered calcifications posterior to the right nipple was completed; the formal localization report was reviewed after surgery, but only the procedure record is used at this time.

critical_omission_rules_en: It must be stated that permanent pathological results have not yet been disclosed.
Pathology-result review and continuous breast-surgery follow-up must be arranged.
Routine postoperative observation, incision care, and return-to-hospital instructions must be completed.

stopping.rationale_en: The planned right breast quadrantectomy is complete, frozen section supports benign disease, and postoperative vital signs and wound status are stable without recorded infection or drainage. Therefore, discharge and follow-up are reasonable after standard discharge criteria and instructions are completed; tracking of permanent pathology must not stop, and the result should be reviewed by breast surgery when available.
remaining_blockers_en: Formal permanent pathology results have not yet been disclosed, and final diagnostic closure has not been completed

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.
